cells.tense: The structure is going up now and the hands are still on it.
cells.act: show someone the way you found
cells.ask: With one person stuck at the point you already got past, put the route down in plain words and then go quiet about it — no doubling back to check.
cells.core:
You're at the part where work gets finished well enough to leave your hands. It's going without strain, because you're trusting the form to hold rather than guarding it. What you built is integrated, and the finishing opens instead of closing. New structure is emerging in how you think about the work, the first frame of it, and it comes out of the hands-on part rather than the plans.

The way back moves through other people, and it looks like plain direction. You spent real effort learning this route; someone behind you on the same stretch hasn't. Put down where the passage is and go quiet. The telling won't thin you — solitude on the way back connects instead of isolating, and refining your own work could turn into gripping. Here it doesn't, because you're willing to hand it on.

cells.verb: building something new from what the clearing left standing
cells.place: the threshold where finished work becomes the next beginning

cells.tense: The finished version is being lived in already, ahead of the hands.
cells.act: walk toward what connects, leaving what does not
cells.ask: Drop the piece you keep re-adding out of habit, even though nobody living uses it — take it out of the next version by your own hand.
cells.core:
You're at the crossing point and already living past it. The final form is in your head, so the raising feels behind schedule and the hands get pushed past what the thing can hold. What you're defending isn't the work; it's a shape that hasn't arrived. The last step keeps getting thrown over the top of the one under it.

What brings you back is going toward the connection that's still live — the people this is actually for — and letting the rest fall away. The piece you keep adding because it was once right, or because cutting it feels like loss, is the piece that no longer travels. Take out one of those by your own hand and watch what the live connection does with the space that opens.

cells.tense: The old structures came down and nothing new has risen since.
cells.act: decide it and act the same day, without explaining
cells.ask: Make the next call on this build and carry it through before the day ends — nobody is told, nobody is given a reason.
cells.core:
You can see the cleared ground and you stand at the far side of it. The old structures came down — you know exactly where they were — and nothing is going up on the space. You can describe what should be raised; you just don't start. The not-starting has gone on long enough that it feels like judgment rather than fear.

What's called for doesn't require you to feel like building. Make the call and carry it through the same day. Small, no announcement, no reasons given to anybody. Real authority doesn't assert itself — it moves, and the structure does the talking. This first move doesn't have to be right. It has to be made, because making it is the only thing that puts ground back under your feet.

cells.tense: The build is underway and your telling credits it to circumstance.
cells.act: keep the heading when it is contested
cells.ask: Somebody questions where this is going — let the course stand exactly as it is, through that conversation, without mounting a case for it.
cells.core:
You're building, and you credit the build to luck. Asked how it came together, you say it came together — you had the opportunity, the pieces happened to fit. Meanwhile the direction is genuinely yours: the choices, the order of them, the refusal of the easier shape. Your hand decided. Your account of it leaves the hand out.

What's needed is older than you think. Before the build there was a want — a pull toward a particular thing that the structure now carries — and it's still what moves you when you let it. Feel for what you actually want here and keep the heading from there. Momentum isn't gathered by pushing; it's harvested from engagement. What you're engaged with has been yours the whole time.

attempts.check: Unsupported claim: that the person is at the moment of finishing or releasing anything — the record shows the seat, not that arrival is happening. A reader could say the building is long done and nothing is being released, so the core should describe the capacity as it shows up now rather than assert a stage they are in. The asks survive being wrong because each is a small visible act (a page, one piece down, one same-day call, one heading kept) useful even if the read misses. The sentence that serves me more than them is any 'you are at the threshold' phrasing — cut; the cores point at what the capacity does, not where I place them.
